Formulation
- Predisposing factors: No psychiatric predisposing factors recorded; history of asthma only.
- Precipitating factors: Onset 3 days ago after a takeaway meal eaten ~4 days ago; likely infectious gastroenteritis.
- Perpetuating factors: Continuing to attend work despite symptoms; reduced oral intake; frequent diarrhea limiting mobility.
- Protective factors: Able to maintain fluid intake; family support at home; clinician provided conservative management plan and safety-netting.
- Summary: Patient presents with a provisional diagnosis of acute gastroenteritis causing frequent watery diarrhea, intermittent left-sided lower abdominal cramping, initial vomiting, subjective fever, and reduced appetite. Symptoms have impacted occupational functioning. Conservative management (oral rehydration, paracetamol, rest) and sick leave are advised with safety-netting for persistence.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute gastroenteritis (provisional)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce diarrhea and vomiting
  - Restore strength and appetite
  - Return to usual work and activities
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Prevent dehydration and complications
  - Symptomatic relief (pain/fever control)
  - Reassess if symptoms persist or worsen; identify alternative causes if not resolving within expected timeframe
- Actions (Patient):
  - Maintain oral fluids; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as available
  - Take paracetamol as advised ("two tablets up to four times a day" as discussed) for fever/aches
  - Rest and take time off work for 2–3 days as advised
  - Monitor symptoms and return for review if no improvement within 3–4 days or if symptoms worsen
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Advise conservative management: hydration, oral rehydration solution, paracetamol for fever/aches
  - Recommend 2–3 days off work to rest
  - Safety-net: review if symptoms persist at 3–4 days and consider stool testing if ongoing
  - No antibiotics prescribed at this stage

Secondary Problem: Functional impact on work and daily activities
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Be able to attend work without frequent interruption by symptoms
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Reduce symptom burden to enable return to work safely
- Actions (Patient):
  - Follow recommended rest period; stay close to suitable facilities while symptoms persist
  - Communicate with employer regarding sick leave as advised
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide advice/support for 2–3 days off work
  - Reassess occupational fitness at follow-up if needed

Tertiary Problem: Risk of dehydration / reduced oral intake
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Maintain adequate fluid and electrolyte balance
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Prevent dehydration; restore adequate oral intake
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take oral rehydration solutions (Dioralyte) and clear fluids; eat light foods as tolerated
  - Avoid alcohol and smoking (patient already does)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Advise on use of Dioralyte; monitor for signs of dehydration; arrange review if unable to maintain fluids

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Explanation of likely diagnosis (gastroenteritis/tummy bug)
  - Advice to maintain hydration; recommendation of oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte)
  - Use of paracetamol for fever/aches (dose as discussed)
  - Rest and time off work for 2–3 days
  - Safety-netting: return if symptoms persist at 3–4 days; possibility of stool testing if ongoing
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Not explicitly listed; clinician advised to return if symptoms have not improved within 3–4 days or if symptoms worsen (implies need to seek further care)
- Coping Strategies:
  - Rest, stay hydrated, consume light/liquid foods as tolerated

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes — patient stated plan was clear and agreed
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date:
